paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the will of God is a better thing to live for than anything your old crowd is chasing. Peter says Christ suffered in His body, so arm yourselves with the same resolve (1 Peter 4:1). Your remaining time on earth isn't for human passions, but for the will of God (1 Peter 4:2). And yes, some folks will think it's strange and heap abuse on you, but they will have to give an account to Him who is ready to judge the living and the dead (1 Peter 4:4-5).

Now, how do you live it? Peter says the end of all things is near, so be clear-minded and sober, so that you can pray (1 Peter 4:7). Then he says, "Above all, love one another deeply, because love covers over a multitude of sins" (1 Peter 4:8). Open your door without complaining, friend, because I've sat in a dark drawer, and I know what a warm welcome is worth (1 Peter 4:9). I'm not saying that's the only thing you do. I'm saying Peter put it ABOVE ALL!

And you're not doing it on your own battery. Each of you has a gift, and you're a steward of the manifold grace of God, so use it to serve one another (1 Peter 4:10). Speak as one conveying the words of God, and serve with the strength God provides (1 Peter 4:11). Why? "…so that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ…" (1 Peter 4:11). So go bake something good for somebody today, baker, and let Him get the glory.
